text: What happens if you fall into a black hole?
At first, it's beautiful. Gas swirls around it at nearly the speed of light, glowing millions of degrees hot.
Its gravity is so strong, it bends light. You can see the back of the disk, wrapped over the top.
Your feet are pulled harder than your head.
Near a small black hole, you'd be stretched like a noodle.
But near a giant one, you could cross the edge and feel nothing at all.
To a friend watching from far away, you'd slow down, turn red, and freeze at the edge.
But for you, there's no way back. Not even light can escape.
